articles.title: PHP2Shell: Why Patch Available Is Not Fleet Verified
articles.excerpt: The PHP project released fixes for two critical core vulnerabilities on October 21, 2026: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Both can permit unauthenticated remote code execution under demonstrated…
articles.body: The PHP project released fixes for two critical core vulnerabilities on October 21, 2026: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Both can permit unauthenticated remote code execution under demonstrated conditions. The urgent technical instruction is straightforward: follow PHP's official advisory and your distribution or LTS vendor's guidance, then update to a verified fixed build. Configuration-only mitigations reduce exposure to particular paths but do not fully resolve both flaws. The harder operational lesson is that a patch release is not evidence that every running system is fixed . The response clock started before public disclosure Amazon Threat Intelligence reports that its MadPot sensors observed an exploitation attempt dated October 17—four calendar days before public disclosure.
articles.author: Ariftly

articles.title: Email Risk Score: Signals That Flag Fraud at Signup
articles.excerpt: Fraud teams use it at signup to decide whether to approve, step up verification, or review, rather than to decline outright. Every digital lender, BNPL app, and marketplace asks for an email address a…
articles.body: Fraud teams use it at signup to decide whether to approve, step up verification, or review, rather than to decline outright. Every digital lender, BNPL app, and marketplace asks for an email address at signup. Most treat it as a contact field. Fraud teams increasingly treat it as evidence, and an email risk score turns that evidence into a decision: an address created ten minutes ago on a throwaway domain says something different from a five-year-old mailbox on a company domain. This guide explains what goes into an email risk score , how each signal works technically, which ones are reliable, and how to turn them into proportionate decisions that block abuse without turning away genuine customers.

articles.title: Writing a README People Actually Read: Notes From a Writer Learning to Code
articles.excerpt: I'm learning to code. Along the way I've noticed something: the part of a project I understand fastest is usually the README. When a README is unclear, I often give up before I ever open the code. Wri…
articles.body: I'm learning to code. Along the way I've noticed something: the part of a project I understand fastest is usually the README. When a README is unclear, I often give up before I ever open the code. Writing is the part I'm comfortable with, so here are the habits I keep coming back to when I read (and try to write) READMEs. Start with one sentence that says what it is The first line should answer "what is this, and who is it for?" Most visitors decide within seconds whether to keep reading. A sentence like "A command-line tool that renames photos by the date they were taken" does more work than three paragraphs of background. Show it working before you explain it People want to see the result first.

articles.title: I vibe-coded a Pebble Time 2 app, and I learned some tough lessons
articles.excerpt: It's not as simple as it looks.
articles.body: If you spend enough time on the internet, you’ll be led to believe coding is now easy for everyone thanks to various AI models. Claude, ChatGPT, and others can turn even a novice into a master programmer, and software engineers should seriously consider a second career as pastry chefs. Unsurprisingly, that’s a gross mischaracterization. Large language models do give people without formal training tools they could’ve never imagined before, but it’s not that simple. So, I decided to find out for myself. I recently wrote about how much I love my Pebble Time 2 , and part of the appeal is PebbleOS. It’s open-source, and people can write their own programs to fit their needs. I decided to lean heavily on nostalgia and see if I could recreate the Microsoft MSN Direct service from the mid-2000s.

articles.title: Anime's Most Devastating Horror Story Is a Tragedy About Being Human
articles.excerpt: Devilman Crybaby is a brutal anime that transforms the end of the world into a nightmare about what makes us human.
articles.body: But if you're looking for an anime that understands how horror can be both visually repulsive and emotionally devastating, Devilman Crybaby is the perfect series for you. Released on Netflix in 2018, Masaaki Yuasa's 10-episode adaptation of Go Nagai's Devilman is a spectacularly gruesome descent into the apocalypse. At its center is Akira Fudo, a sensitive young man forced into a horrific union with a demon to defend humankind from an existential threat. Granted immense power without sacrificing his empathy, Akira becomes a walking paradox: a creature born of unimaginable violence who still weeps for mankind. This core tension that propels the narrative, probing the fragile line between humanity and monstrosity.

articles.body: TL;DR Google has told Android Authority that it’s looking to bring sleep breathing quality to the Fitbit Edge. The tracker already supports blood pressure and insulin resistance trends through Google Health Premium, but it still lacks the sleep feature. Unlike the Fitbit Air, which Google says will get the feature soon, support for the Fitbit Edge doesn’t seem guaranteed yet. The Fitbit Edge has plenty going for it as Google’s long-awaited successor to the Charge lineup. articles.body: The state of the smartphone market in 2026 is quietly getting quite worrying. Sure, we have Apple finally jumping onto the foldable phone bandwagon with the iPhone Duo , and brands like OPPO and vivo continue to deliver some excellent camera smartphones . But there’s no denying that rising memory prices, and consequently higher smartphone prices, are starting to affect the market. Samsung recently increased the prices of its Galaxy S26 series , which means even the base Galaxy S26 now starts at a whopping $1,000 in the US. And the impact is starting to show in sales figures as well, with the smartphone market reportedly seeing a 20% decline in sales , the biggest drop in nearly 14 years.

articles.title: Faster to Science: A Letter to the Science Community
articles.excerpt: NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall.
articles.body: Dear NASA Science Community, NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall, from NASA Headquarters, to explain our new Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), and answer your questions. We have heard you. We have listened. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long. It has taken years to move mission concepts through the current two-step process. This has often come with contract management challenges, unpredictability, and not enough funding. NASA is committed to doing better — and I’m excited to share with you how we’re making it happen.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year.
